_licensingNote: Original, not an SCP. This file is an Incident Package manifest — the unit GDD §25.8 states the content-lock gate at — and it binds an anomaly, a map and a premise that are all first-party to this project. licensingRecordId is null because there is no third-party material in the package to record, and this note is what makes that null mean 'checked, and here is why' rather than 'nobody has looked at this one'. §25.7's ShareAlike questions do not engage. The gate status and §25.3's field table are in content/provenance.json.
_note:
THE THIRD PACKAGE, AND THE ONE THAT PROVES THE MODEL WORKS IN THE OTHER DIRECTION (GDD 15.1, 26.2). The first two are one anomaly each on one shared floor: same building, different thing. This is the same THING on a different building — the graybox-draught again, with every rule in its file untouched, on geometry that makes those rules mean something else.

The cold store's aisles are 4.2m and a floodlight's 40C contour is 3.375m across, so a lane needs two posts and heat is the scarce resource. Ashlar's heating gallery is 2.400m wide, so one post closes the tube across and only its two ends are left: heat is cheap here and the JOURNEY is what costs. A squad that learned 'bring four tripods' brings four tripods nine floors up a condemned block for no reason, and a squad that learned 'the fence is made of heat' has not noticed that the last lane here has to be closed with something cold, because a tripod set 3.6m from the transit case lifts the case past 40C and the bait stops working. That is what the doors are for.

This map is also the first one where the anomalySpawn and evidenceSources live ONLY here. ashlar-house-9.json is pure geometry — it does not know what happened in it.
_variationNote:
GDD §14.4. Ashlar varies in the WALK, because the walk is what this floor charges for. A jammed lobby door closes the only cross-link in the middle of the plan and turns a lap into a full circuit; a faulted landing circuit means the lobby never opens at all and the squad pays the long way round for the whole operation — which is a harder night and never an impossible one, because the loop is the loop.

⚠ THE GALLERY CIRCUIT IS NOT ON THE FAULT LIST AND THE GALLERY DOORS ARE NOT ON THE ROUTE LIST. Both are the containment: the fire-stopping door is worth exactly one tripod and the lane door is the lane. A seed that faulted the gallery would make the authored pen unbuildable, which is precisely the unwinnable state §14.4 forbids — and it would arrive one night in four with nothing to say it had.

briefing.headline: Cold complaint, condemned block, ninth floor
briefing.report: Ashlar House was decanted eleven months ago and is due for demolition. A strip-out contractor pulled his crew off the ninth floor after two of them 'walked into a cold that followed'. His day book is still at the temporary board in the heating gallery, where he left it.

known.text: The site watchman is on the east landing and will let you up.
Both circuits on this floor are on the contractor's temporaries, not the mains.
The district-heating gallery was drained and capped four years ago and runs the full width of the floor.
The watchman puts the first complaint three weeks before the contractor's, in a flat on the north side.

_evidenceNote:
GDD §27.2 wants two evidence paths per required rule, and the count that matters is the one taken ON THIS FLOOR. The first six sources here are the six the cold store's list could honestly be re-sited into; the other five of the anomaly's twelve are cold-store fiction — a chart recorder on a plant wall, two lamps eleven metres apart in an aisle, a four-way charging rack in the bay — and a condemned crosswall block stripped to its frame contains none of those things. Placing them anyway would have turned the scorecard green by writing something false into the floor, so the five below were AUTHORED instead, out of what this building actually has: a strip-out contractor's paperwork, his fire point, his temporary alarm, and the block's own frost protection.

MEASURED, against the real Site with EVERY DOOR SHUT and an operative radius of 0.34m. Each of the five is standable, at least 2.8m from every other source on the floor so two prompts never compete for one keypress, at least 3m from every door centre, breaker, the cargo cache and the extraction point so the evidence verb never competes with a fixture verb, outside the authored pen and off every authored origin. Wall clearance / nearest source / nearest fixture, in metres: permit book 1.34 / 7.41 / 3.85 · frost heaters 0.83 / 4.62 / 3.45 · accident book 1.44 / 3.40 / 4.00 · fire-watch camera 1.44 / 3.20 / 4.39 · call point 1.10 / 5.98 / 3.86. All five are walkable from the squad's spawn with the doors as the map ships them.

The spread is deliberate and it is the map's own argument: the permit book, the heaters and the fire point are down in the store rooms on the way to the gallery, and the accident book and the call point are at the far north end. This floor charges for the WALK, so a squad that wants a second path on every rule pays a full circuit for it.
